card: Describe a friend or acquaintance who is good at something.
pts: and explain how it has affected you
model:
I'd like to talk about an old school friend who is remarkably good at drawing. We've known each other since primary school, and although we now study different subjects, we still meet regularly.

He can draw almost anything: portraits, buildings, even complicated maps from memory. If you give him a pen and a piece of paper, he'll produce something impressive within minutes.

As far as I know, he developed this ability through a lot of practice. When he was about ten, his uncle gave him a sketchbook, and since then he has drawn every day. He also watched online tutorials and copied the work of artists he liked. According to him, the secret is to do a little every day rather than a lot once a week.

His talent has influenced me in a couple of ways. Firstly, he designed the logo for a small project of mine, and it looked far more professional than anything I could have done. Secondly, and more importantly, he has shown me what regular practice can achieve. After watching him, I decided to set aside thirty minutes every morning to improve my writing in English.

I suppose that's the best thing about having talented friends: they quietly push you to become better yourself.
tipAr: عبارات التخفيف مثل As far as I know وI suppose تجعل كلامك طبيعياً وتحميك من تقديم معلومات مؤكدة لا تعرفها.

card: Describe a historical place you have visited.
pts: when and why you visited it
and explain what you learnt from the visit
model:
The historical place I'd like to describe is an ancient Roman site not far from my hometown, with stone streets, broken columns and a large open-air theatre. It is one of the best-preserved sites in the region.

I visited it about three years ago on a school trip organised by our history teacher. The purpose was to help us understand how people lived in the area two thousand years ago, and, to be honest, I wasn't expecting much. I thought it would be a boring day of listening to explanations.

However, as soon as I entered the theatre, my opinion changed. We could see the rows of seats curving upwards, and the guide explained that the acoustics were so good that someone speaking on the stage could be heard at the very top without shouting. We also walked along the main road, where you can still see the marks of cart wheels in the stones, and visited the remains of public baths.

What I learnt is that ancient societies were far more organised than we usually imagine. They had water systems, laws about trade and even public buildings for justice. It made me realise that many of the ideas we discuss today, such as fair rules for everyone, have very deep roots.

The visit really sparked my interest in history, and I've been back twice since.
phr: to be honest, I wasn't expecting much
far more organised than we usually imagine
tipAr: يمكنك ربط المكان التاريخي باهتماماتك (القانون، العدالة) فهذا يجعل إجابتك شخصية ومميزة.

card: Describe a park or green space in your area.
pts: and explain how important it is for the local community
model:
I'd like to describe the main public garden in my town, which lies at the foot of a small hill, about ten minutes' walk from the town centre. It was opened some thirty years ago and has been improved several times since.

It's quite a large space with tall palm trees, long paths and plenty of benches. There is a small fountain in the middle, surrounded by flower beds, and at the far end there is a playground for children. In spring, the whole garden fills with colour and the smell of orange blossom.

People use it in many different ways. Early in the morning, you'll see older men walking slowly and chatting about the news. Around five o'clock, families arrive with their children, and teenagers play football on the grass. Some students, like me, go there with a book to revise for exams in the shade.

I believe it plays an essential role in the community. In a crowded town with many tall buildings, it offers a place to breathe and relax. It also brings people of different ages together, which doesn't happen very often elsewhere. Moreover, it's free, so everyone can enjoy it regardless of their income.

For all these reasons, I think local authorities should invest even more in places like this.
tipAr: عند الحديث عن أهمية مكان للمجتمع اذكر فائدتين على الأقل: صحية واجتماعية، فهذا يعطي عمقاً للنقطة الأخيرة.

card: Describe an article or film that changed the way you think about something.
pts: when and where you came across it
and explain how it changed your opinion
model:
I'd like to talk about a documentary on how public money is spent, which I watched about a year and a half ago. A lecturer recommended it, and I watched it one evening in my room on my laptop.

The film follows several journalists who investigate why a hospital in a poor district never received the equipment that had been paid for. Step by step, they trace the money through contracts, offices and companies, and they discover that the paperwork was changed along the way. What impressed me was that they relied on documents and data rather than rumours.

Before watching it, I used to think that corruption was something obvious, like someone openly taking an envelope. However, the documentary showed me that it's often hidden in complicated procedures that most people never read. That completely changed my perspective. I realised that transparency is not only about punishing people; it's also about designing systems where it's hard to cheat in the first place.

As a result, I became more interested in how technology and open data can help to detect problems early. In fact, it was one of the main reasons I chose my current field of study.

So, in a way, a single film shaped the direction of my education.
tipAr: عبارة I used to think... However, ... أسلوب ممتاز لوصف تغيّر الرأي، وتتكرر كثيراً في أسئلة الجزء الثاني.

card: Describe a gift you received that was important to you.
pts: and explain why it was important to you
model:
The gift I'd like to talk about is a second-hand laptop that my older brother gave me when I started university. It wasn't new, and the keyboard had a few worn keys, but it meant the world to me.

He handed it to me about four years ago, on the evening before I left for the dormitory. We were sitting in the living room, and he said, I bought this with my first salary, and now it's your turn to use it well. I remember the moment clearly because he was always shy about showing his feelings.

At that time, my family couldn't afford a new computer, so I had been worried about how I would do my assignments. This laptop solved that problem immediately. I used it to write essays, to attend online lectures and, later on, to learn programming and start my research.

Its importance for me is both practical and emotional. Practically, without it I would have struggled much more during my first years. Emotionally, it reminds me that someone believed in me before I had achieved anything.

Even though I've since bought a better machine, I still keep the old one in my drawer, and I will probably never throw it away.
phr: it meant the world to me
tipAr: تفاصيل صغيرة مثل جملة قالها الشخص أو مكان تسليم الهدية تجعل القصة مقنعة وتساعدك على الاسترسال.

card: Describe an important event in your life that you celebrated.
pts: and explain why it was important
model:
The event I'd like to describe is my graduation from my bachelor's degree. It took place in July, a little over a year ago, and it was without doubt one of the proudest days of my life.

The ceremony was held in the university's main hall, and my parents, my two sisters and a couple of close friends came to support me. My mother had bought a new dress for the occasion, and my father wore his best suit, which he normally keeps for weddings.

During the ceremony, we all wore long gowns and square hats, and each of us was called to the stage to receive a certificate. When my name was announced, I could hear my sisters clapping loudly from the back. Afterwards, we took dozens of photos in the garden, and the whole family went to a restaurant for a late lunch.

The reason this day mattered so much is that it represented years of effort, late nights and sacrifices, not just mine but also my family's. I was the first person in my family to finish a university degree, so for my parents it was a dream come true.

Looking back, I think that day gave me the motivation I needed to continue studying, and I still keep the certificate on my desk.
phr: I was called to the stage
tipAr: أعطِ تفاصيل حسية (الملابس، التصفيق، الصور) ثم اشرح الأهمية العاطفية؛ هذا يجمع بين الوصف والتعليل.

card: Describe a time when you had to convince someone to do something.
pts: what you wanted them to do
and explain how you felt about the result
model:
I'd like to talk about the time I convinced my father to let me study away from home. He had always preferred that I stay in my hometown, so when I told him I'd like to enrol in a university in another city, he was not pleased.

It happened about five years ago, just after I'd passed my final school exams. He was worried about the cost, and he also felt that I was too young to live alone.

To persuade him, I prepared carefully. First, I made a simple budget, showing that the expenses were manageable if I shared a room with other students. Then I asked my uncle, whom my father respects a lot, to talk to him. Finally, I promised to call every evening and visit every other weekend. I spoke calmly and listened to his fears instead of arguing.

After about a week, he agreed on one condition: that I would study seriously. I was overjoyed, but also a little nervous, because suddenly I had a big responsibility to live up to.

Looking back, I'm happy I handled it patiently. If I had simply insisted, we might have ended up with a bad atmosphere at home. Instead, he became one of my strongest supporters.
tipAr: عند وصف الإقناع اذكر الخطوات (أعددتُ، طلبتُ مساعدة، وعدتُ) ثم النتيجة؛ ولا تنسَ الحديث عن مشاعرك في النهاية.

card: Describe a project you would like to start in the future.
pts: what you would need to do
and explain why you would like to do it
model:
One project I'd really love to start is a free online platform where ordinary people can check how public money is spent in their town. It would show things like road repairs, school buildings and local contracts in a simple, easy-to-read format.

I would begin with a small team of three or four people: a developer, a designer and a researcher who understands public procurement. Ideally, I would also involve a lawyer to make sure that everything we publish is accurate and legal. Later, we could invite volunteers from universities to help us collect data.

In terms of what I'd have to do, the first step would be to learn more about open data and which documents are publicly available. After that, I'd build a basic version of the website and test it in one town only. If it worked, we could gradually extend it to other regions. Of course, I'd also need some funding, so I'd apply for small grants.

The reason I'm so keen on this idea is that many people feel powerless when they don't know where the money goes. If information were easier to understand, citizens could ask better questions.

I realise it's an ambitious plan, but I think it's well worth trying, and I've already started taking notes.
phr: One project I'd really love to start is...
In terms of what I'd have to do,
The reason I'm so keen on... is that...
tipAr: في الحديث عن المستقبل استعمل would وcould وif + الماضي، مثل If information were easier to understand...

card: Describe a job you would like to do in the future.
pts: what skills or qualifications you would need
and explain why you would like this job
model:
The job I'd really like to do one day is university lecturer and researcher in the field of law and technology. I would like to study how artificial intelligence can be used in courts and in analysing legal cases, and also teach young students about it.

As for the work itself, it would involve three main things. First, I'd carry out research and publish articles. Second, I would prepare and give lectures, and finally I'd supervise students who are writing their own theses. There would also be conferences, where I could meet other researchers from different countries.

In terms of qualifications, I'd need a doctorate, ideally from a well-known university abroad. I would also need strong academic writing skills, a good level of English and, in my case, a basic understanding of programming so I can follow the technical side. On top of that, patience is essential, because research can be slow.

The reason this job appeals to me is that it combines my three main interests: law, technology and learning. Moreover, I believe good research can help societies become fairer and more efficient.

It's a long road, but I'm working towards it step by step.
phr: The job I'd really like to do one day is...
The reason this job appeals to me is that...
tipAr: استعمل In terms of وAs for لتنظيم الإجابة حول النقاط الأربع، فهي تُظهر لغة أكاديمية مناسبة لمستوى B2.

card: Describe a law or rule you think should be introduced.
pts: what the law or rule would be
and explain how it would benefit people
model:
If I could introduce a new law, it would be one that requires every public institution to publish its main contracts and budgets online in a simple format. I think it should apply in my own country, but it could work anywhere.

The way it would work is quite simple. Every ministry, city council and public company would have to upload basic information within thirty days: who received the contract, how much it cost, and when the work should be finished. Citizens could search the information for free, and an independent office would check that institutions respect the deadline. Those who failed to publish would face a fine.

I believe that the benefits would be considerable. Firstly, it would make it harder to hide wasteful or dishonest decisions, because anyone, including journalists and students, could examine the data. Secondly, honest companies would have a fairer chance to compete, since they'd know that the process is visible to everyone. Finally, people would trust public institutions more, which is essential for any healthy society.

Of course, there could be difficulties at the beginning, such as a lack of training or technical problems. Nevertheless, I'm convinced that the long-term advantages would outweigh them.

In short, openness is one of the simplest and cheapest ways to improve public life.
phr: If I could introduce a new law, it would be...
The way it would work is...
the long-term advantages would outweigh them
tipAr: في أسئلة القوانين استعمل الجملة الشرطية الثانية (If I could..., it would...) ثم اشرح آلية التطبيق والفائدة.
